claim: When you initiate restore requests for objects in S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval, S3 Glacier Deep Archive or S3 Intelligent-Tiering, a retrieval-requests quota applies to your AWS account: S3 Glacier supports restore requests at a rate of 1,000 transactions per second. Above that rate, otherwise valid requests are throttled or rejected with a ThrottlingException error; S3 Batch Operations can retrieve many objects with a single request.

qualifiers.condition: RestoreObject requests for S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval, S3 Glacier Deep Archive or S3 Intelligent-Tiering objects; increased restoration limits through AWS Support

evidence.quote: When you initiate restore requests for objects that are stored in the S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval, S3 Glacier Deep Archive, or S3 Intelligent-Tiering storage classes, a retrieval-requests quota is applied for your AWS account.

S3 Glacier supports restore requests at a rate of 1,000 transactions per second. If this rate is exceeded otherwise valid requests are throttled or rejected and Amazon S3 returns a `ThrottlingException` error. You can use S3 Batch Operations to retrieve many objects with a single request, which fully utilizes the restore request rate available in your account.
If you require increased restoration limits, you can contact AWS Support.
